title: How an Email Redirected a $449K+ House Payment
hook: One email redirected a home-closing wire of over $449,000.
description: A documented August 2025 case from the FBI IC3 2025 Annual Report, page 23. The receiving bank confirmed the full amount was on hold; the report does not say the money was returned. Verify wiring changes through a number you find independently. Source: https://www.ic3.gov/AnnualReport/Reports/2025_IC3Report.pdf ; FBI guidance: https://www.ic3.gov/CrimeInfo/BEC . Recreated visuals are illustrations.

scenes.narration: One email redirected a home-closing wire of over $449,000.
scenes.heading: ONE EMAIL. $449K+
scenes.label: Illustration

scenes.narration: In August 2025, buyers received an email impersonating their real attorneys while they were closing on a home.
scenes.heading: THE EMAIL
scenes.label: Illustration

scenes.narration: They sent the wire to the account in that message. The instructions were fraudulent.
scenes.heading: THE SWITCH
scenes.label: Illustration

scenes.narration: The buyers alerted their bank and filed a complaint with the FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center.
scenes.heading: THE REPORT
scenes.label: Illustration

scenes.narration: The FBI requested a freeze. The receiving bank confirmed the full amount was still there, on hold.
scenes.heading: THE HOLD
scenes.label: Illustration

scenes.narration: The report does not say the money was returned. Catching a false wire before sending is safer.
scenes.heading: THE LIMIT
scenes.label: Illustration

scenes.narration: Before wiring, call your attorney using a number found independently. If you've sent it, call your bank immediately for a recall, then report it at IC3.gov.
scenes.heading: THE RULE
scenes.label: Illustration

notes: IC3 2025 Annual Report PDF page 23 documents the August 2025 impersonation, wire over $449,000, IC3 complaint, FBI freeze request, and full amount on hold.
IC3 BEC page supports independent verification, immediate bank contact and recall request, and IC3 reporting.
